title: Sickle cell variants, hemolytic and aplastic anemia, hemophilia, neutropenia
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's blood disorder (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

HPI
Pt is a 63-year-old female presenting for a scheduled follow-up of warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Pt reports feeling stable over the past month. She denies any acute fatigue, shortness of breath, or yellowing of the eyes/skin. Pt reports adherence to her current prednisone taper. No new symptoms since the last visit.

Medication List
Prednisone 10mg daily (tapering)
Multivitamin daily

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Denies fatigue, weight change.
Skin: Denies pruritus, rashes.
Respiratory: Denies SOB, cough.
CV: Denies chest pain, palpitations.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History
Pt lives in a single-family home with her spouse. Retired. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension, stroke.
Father: Type 2 Diabetes.
Siblings: One brother, healthy.

Recent Labs
Hb: 10.2 g/dL
Hct: 31%
Reticulocyte count: 120,000/uL
Bilirubin: 1.1 mg/dL
LDH: 310 U/L
haptoglobin: 45 mg/dL
eGFR: 78 mL/min

Vitals
BP: 128/82
HR: 74 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
RR: 16
SpO2: 98% on RA
Wt: 155 lbs

Exam
General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3. In no acute distress.
Skin: No jaundice noted. No pallor.
Neck: No lymphadenopathy.
Heart: RRR, regular S1/S2, no murmurs.
Lungs: CTAB.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: No edema.

Assessment
1. Warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Pt is currently stable and asymptomatic. Hematologic parameters show mild anemia, but currently controlled on the prednisone taper.

Plan
1. Continue prednisone 10mg daily.
2. Continue current tapering schedule as discussed.
3. Follow up in 4 weeks for repeat CBC and reticulocyte count.
4. Instructed to call office immediately if she experiences severe fatigue or increased yellowing of skin/eyes.

Electronically signed, T. Haddad, NP, 05/14/2026
